newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian officials to Paris to discuss tsarist debt.
newsitem.headline: Russian officials to Paris to discuss tsarist debt.

text.p: A senior Finance Ministry official will accompany Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to Paris on Monday and discuss the problem of Russian bonds issued in the tsarist era, a Finance Ministry official said on Monday.
Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov is accompanying Chernomyrdin, who will leave later today, and whose visit was announced by the French Foreign Ministry last week.
Kasyanov is the senior official in the ministry responsible for foreign debt. Last week Finance Minister Alexander Livshits was named head of the government commission on foreign debt and assets.
The trip will last until Thursday and Russian officials will make a statement in Paris about the talks, the official said.
The Paris Bourse said on Monday it had suspended trading in Russia's tsarist-era bonds, issued before the 1917 Bolshevik revolution.
French investors were heavy buyers of the bonds.
The Soviet regime refused to meet any obligations of the tsarist government, leaving thousands of French people holding beautiful, but virtually worthless paper.

A council of French bondholders has appealed to the French government for support in the dispute and placed advertisements in the international financial press, in the run up to the launch of Russia's debut Eurobond, warning of the dangers of investing in Russian securities.
Russia assumed responsibility for the debts of the former Soviet Union, but the status of pre-Soviet debt is uncertain.
